_comment: Learn step by step (/step-by-step): the curated beginner path. Tasks reference reviewed items by ref, they never copy text — see src/lib/einfach-content.js for the ref formats and docs/easy-mode-tier1-v1.md for how to add a unit. Check with: pnpm check:einfach. Spanish version (beginner-path run, 2026-11-04): A1, A2 and B1 are playable, units in the order of grammatik-lehrplan.json, except that ser/estar comes before plurals here because the plural unit also needs adjective agreement. Old ids are kept where a unit fits them; new units have English ids. Mostly luecke and satz tasks; hoeren and aussprache tasks wait for their audio; a1-vorstellen and a1-amt each have a redemittel task. Hints and whys are English; the Spanish comes from the source item. No task points at an item with es419.skip, so a LatAm mode loses no task; four items have an es419.form the resolver must apply then (personalpronomen/0/5, aduso/0/1, konjunktiv2-hoeflich/1/2, redemittel begruessen#1). Postcards are written here (source: neu) until Edgar has checked them.

units.title: Introduce yourself
claims: You say hello and say your name.
You use yo, tú, usted and vosotros.

postcard.fact: The Kilómetro Cero is in Madrid, at Puerta del Sol. Spain's main roads count their distance from here.

tasks.hint: Buenos ends in -os. Which word goes with it?
tasks.why: We say buenos días, but buenas tardes and buenas noches.

tasks.hint: Oksana is talking about herself.
tasks.why: Me llamo Oksana = my name is Oksana.
Me llamo + your name. Me comes first.

tasks.hint: Look at the end of the verb: -o.
tasks.why: The ending -o belongs to yo: vivo.

tasks.hint: You ask an older neighbour you do not know.
tasks.why: Someone you do not know: usted. ¿Cómo se llama usted?

tasks.hint: You are talking to two people here in Spain.
tasks.why: In Spain, tú + another person = vosotros.

tasks.situation: You meet a new neighbour for the first time. You have just said your names.
tasks.hint: You are pleased to meet this person.

units.title: Show someone your home
claims: You talk about the things in your home.
You choose el, la, un or una.

postcard.fact: Work on the Sagrada Família began in 1882. Many people have worked on it since then.

tasks.hint: Look at the last letter of mesa.
tasks.why: Most words in -a are feminine: la mesa.

tasks.hint: Look at the last letter of piso.
tasks.why: Most words in -o are masculine: el piso.

tasks.hint: One key is la llave. Here you have more.
tasks.why: La llave, las llaves. The -s means more than one.

tasks.hint: Silla ends in -a. It is one chair.
tasks.why: La silla, so: una silla.

tasks.hint: You talk about this flat for the first time.
tasks.why: Something new: un, una. Vivo en un piso pequeño.

tasks.hint: You both know the home has one.
tasks.why: Something you both know: el, la. ¿Dónde está el baño?

units.title: Say who and where you are
claims: You say who you are with ser.
You say where you are with estar.

postcard.fact: People call Toledo the city of three cultures. Christians, Muslims and Jews lived here for centuries.

tasks.hint: You say where you come from.
tasks.why: Where you come from: ser. Soy de Ucrania.

tasks.hint: The sentence says where it is.
tasks.why: Where something is: estar. La farmacia está en la calle Mayor.

tasks.hint: Profesora is her job.
tasks.why: A job: ser. Mi hermana es profesora.
A job: ser, with no un or una. Soy enfermera.

tasks.hint: How do you feel in the evening?
tasks.why: How you feel now: estar. Estoy cansada.

tasks.hint: The question asks about the time.
tasks.why: The time: ser. Son las ocho.
Where something is: estar. ¿Dónde está + the thing?

units.title: Describe your flat
claims: You say what things are like.
You match words: los pisos caros.

postcard.fact: In Cuenca, old houses hang over the edge of a deep gorge. People call them the casas colgadas.

tasks.hint: Ciudad ends in a consonant.
tasks.why: After a consonant, add -es: ciudades.

tasks.hint: El piso, los pisos: masculine, more than one.
tasks.why: The adjective matches the noun: los pisos son caros.

tasks.hint: La casa: feminine, one.
tasks.why: Mi casa is feminine, so: pequeña.

tasks.hint: Look at the end of the adjective: -e.
tasks.why: Adjectives in -e do not change for la: una casa grande.

tasks.hint: What comes first, the thing or its colour?
tasks.why: The adjective usually comes after the noun: la casa blanca.
The noun comes first, then the adjective: un piso nuevo.

units.title: Go shopping
claims: You understand numbers and prices.
You say how much something costs.

postcard.fact: Valencia is the home of paella. The rice grows close to the city, around La Albufera lake.

tasks.hint: It is more than ten and less than twenty.
tasks.why: Quince = 15. Cinco = 5. Cincuenta = 50.

tasks.hint: Siete is 7. Setenta sounds like siete.
tasks.why: Setenta = 70, from siete. Sesenta = 60, from seis.

tasks.hint: It is one word. Look at the accent.
tasks.why: From 16 to 29, numbers are one word: veintidós.

tasks.hint: In Spain, the comma comes before the cents.
tasks.why: 2,50 € is two euros and fifty cents.

tasks.hint: In Spain, a point marks the thousands.
tasks.why: 1.200 € is one thousand two hundred euros.

tasks.hint: 500 has its own word. Euros are masculine.
tasks.why: 500 is irregular: quinientos euros, quinientas personas.
Cuesta + the number + euros.

units.title: Get to know someone
claims: You ask and answer yes/no questions.
You ask: ¿Dónde? ¿Cuándo? ¿Quién? ¿Cuántos?

postcard.fact: The University of Salamanca began in 1218. It is the oldest university in Spain.

tasks.hint: The person says: I have two.
tasks.why: Tengo dos means yes. Write sí with an accent.

tasks.hint: How do you make the verb negative?
tasks.why: To say no: no + verb. No, no trabajo los sábados.
No comes right before the verb: no trabajo.

tasks.hint: The answer is a place.
tasks.why: A place: ¿Dónde? And the question word has an accent.

tasks.hint: English says “What's your name?”. Spanish is different.
tasks.why: Spanish says “how do you call yourself?”: ¿Cómo te llamas?

tasks.hint: Los hijos: masculine, more than one.
tasks.why: Cuánto matches the noun: ¿Cuántos hijos?
De dónde + verb + usted.

units.title: Talk about your day
claims: You say what you do every day.
You use -ar, -er and -ir verbs.

postcard.fact: The streets of Seville are full of orange trees. The oranges look sweet, but they are very bitter.

tasks.hint: The ending for yo is the same in most verbs.
tasks.why: With yo, the ending is -o: trabajo.

tasks.hint: Vivir is an -ir verb.
tasks.why: -ir verbs with nosotros: -imos. Vivimos.

tasks.hint: Mi marido = él. The verb is trabajar.
tasks.why: With él and ella, -ar verbs end in -a: trabaja.

tasks.hint: The verb is comer. Who eats? Nosotros.
tasks.why: -er verbs with nosotros: -emos. Comemos a las dos.

tasks.hint: The verb is beber. Look at the word yo.
tasks.why: With yo, the ending is -o: bebo.
Mis hijos = ellos, so the verb ends in -an.

units.title: At the health centre
claims: You say: tengo, voy and estoy.
You say your age with tener.

postcard.fact: The river Ebro runs through Zaragoza. The big Basilica del Pilar stands on its bank.

tasks.why: We say: la mano. It ends in -o, but it is feminine.

tasks.hint: Ir is irregular. Estoy shows the person: yo.
tasks.why: Ir with yo: voy.

tasks.hint: English says “is twelve”. Spanish uses another verb.
tasks.why: Age uses tener: mi hija tiene doce años.

tasks.hint: The yo form has a -g-.
tasks.why: Tener with yo: tengo.

tasks.hint: You ask for water. Why?
tasks.why: Tengo sed = I am thirsty. Spanish uses tener here too.

tasks.hint: The sentence says where you are now.
tasks.why: Where you are: estar. Estamos en el centro de salud.
Ir with nosotros: vamos. And a + el = al.

units.title: In a café
claims: You order: quiero, pido.
You ask: ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta?

postcard.fact: In Asturias, people pour cider from high above the glass. They call this escanciar.

tasks.hint: The verb is querer. The e changes with yo.
tasks.why: Querer: e → ie with yo. Quiero.

tasks.hint: Does the vowel change with nosotros?
tasks.why: With nosotros the stem does not change: queremos.

tasks.hint: The verb is pedir, and you are talking about yourself.
tasks.why: Pedir: e → i with yo. Pido.

tasks.hint: The verb is entender, and you are talking about yourself.
tasks.why: Entender: e → ie with yo. No entiendo.

tasks.hint: The verb is poder, and you ask a friend.
tasks.why: Poder: o → ue with tú. ¿Puedes?
Puedo + the infinitive: pagar does not change.

units.title: Find your way
claims: You ask: ¿Dónde está…? ¿Hay…?
You choose hay, está or están.

postcard.fact: The Camino de Santiago ends here. People walk for days or weeks to reach the cathedral.

tasks.hint: You do not know if there is one.
tasks.why: You do not know if it exists: ¿Hay…? And hay takes una, not la.

tasks.hint: You know there is one. You need the place.
tasks.why: You know it exists: ¿Dónde está…?

tasks.hint: Look at the word un.
tasks.why: Hay + un, una, a number or no article.

tasks.hint: We know the park. The sentence says where it is.
tasks.why: El, la, mi + thing: está. El parque está cerca.

tasks.hint: Look at the word hay.
tasks.why: After hay: un, una. ¿Hay un cajero por aquí?
A known thing + está + the place.

units.title: Talk about your family
claims: You talk about your family.
You say mi, tu, su and nuestro.

postcard.fact: The name of Granada's Alhambra comes from Arabic. It means “the red one”.

tasks.hint: Yo, and one sister.
tasks.why: One thing, and it is yours: mi. Mi hermana.

tasks.hint: Look at padres: one or more than one?
tasks.why: Su + one thing, sus + more. Sus padres.

tasks.hint: Whose wife? Pablo's. How many?
tasks.why: Pablo y su mujer: one wife, so su.

tasks.hint: La hija: feminine, one.
tasks.why: Nuestro matches the noun, not the people: nuestra hija.

tasks.hint: English says “Javier's car”. Spanish has no 's.
tasks.why: Thing + de + owner: el coche de Javier.
Mis + more than one: mis padres.

units.title: Say what you like
claims: You say what you like.
You point at things: este, esta, estos.

postcard.fact: The Guggenheim Museum in Bilbao opened in 1997. Its curved walls shine with titanium.

tasks.hint: El café is one thing.
tasks.why: One thing or a verb: gusta.

tasks.hint: Los perros: how many?
tasks.why: More than one thing: gustan.

tasks.hint: Carmen is one person, not you.
tasks.why: For one other person, the word is le: a Carmen le gusta.

tasks.hint: The first sentence has no. You agree.
tasks.why: After a sentence with no, agree with tampoco.

tasks.hint: Los zapatos: masculine, more than one.
tasks.why: Este, esta, estos, estas match the noun: estos zapatos.

tasks.hint: We say la foto, with la.
tasks.why: Foto ends in -o, but it is feminine: estas fotos.
No + me + gusta + a verb in the infinitive.

units.title: Make an appointment
claims: You say the time: son las diez.
You say when: el lunes, a las diez.

postcard.fact: The Roman aqueduct of Segovia is about 2,000 years old. Its stones stand without any mortar.

tasks.hint: It is 15 minutes after the hour.
tasks.why: Up to half past: y. 6:15 = las seis y cuarto.

tasks.hint: The question is: what time is it?
tasks.why: What time is it? Son las + the hour (la una: es la).

tasks.hint: The question is: at what time?
tasks.why: At what time? A las + the hour.

tasks.hint: One Friday: this Friday.
tasks.why: One day: el viernes. There is no word for “on”.

tasks.hint: Every Sunday, not just one.
tasks.why: Every week: los domingos.
The day takes el: el martes.

units.title: Book the padrón
claims: You ask for an appointment for the padrón.
You say where you live.

postcard.fact: Melilla is a Spanish city in North Africa. It lies on the coast, next to Morocco.

tasks.hint: We say la cita. You ask for one.
tasks.why: La cita, so: una cita.

tasks.hint: The answer is a day.
tasks.why: A day or a time: ¿Cuándo?

tasks.hint: It says at what time.
tasks.why: At what time: a las. La cita es a las nueve y media.

tasks.hint: It says the place where you live.
tasks.why: Vivir + en: vivo en la calle Mayor.

tasks.situation: At the town hall, the clerk tells you the date of your padrón appointment, but you did not catch it.
tasks.hint: You want to hear it again, politely.

tasks.why: Una cita para…: an appointment for something.
A known place: ¿Dónde está + the place?

units.title: Say why
claims: You join ideas with y, o and pero.
You give a reason with porque.

postcard.fact: San Sebastián has two names. In Basque, the city is called Donostia.

tasks.hint: The person has both children.
tasks.why: To add something: y.

tasks.hint: You must choose one drink.
tasks.why: To choose: o. ¿Agua o zumo?

tasks.hint: Small is bad. Cheap is good.
tasks.why: Two ideas that contrast: pero.

tasks.hint: The second part is the reason.
tasks.why: A reason: porque, one word and no accent.

tasks.hint: The answer gives a reason. Now ask for it.
tasks.why: The question is por qué. The answer is porque.
The reason comes after porque.

units.title: Talk about your morning
claims: You talk about your daily routine.
You say: me levanto, te acuestas, se ducha.

postcard.fact: Mount Teide on Tenerife is the highest mountain in Spain, at 3,715 metres.

tasks.hint: Look at the word yo.
tasks.why: Levantarse with yo: me levanto.

tasks.hint: Acuestas: who is it? The -as ending tells you.
tasks.why: The ending -as belongs to tú: te acuestas.

tasks.hint: Mi hermana y yo: who is that together?
tasks.why: Mi hermana y yo = nosotros: nos duchamos.

tasks.hint: Who gets dressed here? The children, not me.
tasks.why: The action goes to another person, so there is no me.

tasks.hint: Yo must get up. The pronoun goes on the end.
tasks.why: After tengo que, the pronoun joins the infinitive: levantarme.
The pronoun goes before the verb: me levanto.

units.title: Plan your week
claims: You say what you are going to do.
You use ir a: voy a llamar.

postcard.fact: The Canary Islands are one hour behind mainland Spain. The radio says: “una hora menos en Canarias”.

tasks.hint: Look at the word yo.
tasks.why: Ir with yo: voy. Voy a llamar.

tasks.hint: Look at the word tú.
tasks.why: Ir with tú: vas. ¿Qué vas a hacer?

tasks.hint: You need three parts: ir, a, and an infinitive.
tasks.why: Ir + a + infinitive: voy a ir.

tasks.hint: After a, the verb does not change.
tasks.why: After a comes the infinitive: voy a cambiar.

tasks.hint: Sale is one person. Keep that person.
tasks.why: Sale → va a salir. The second verb is the infinitive.
Don't forget the a: voy a llamar.

units.title: Say what you are doing
claims: You say what you are doing now.
You choose: every day or right now.

postcard.fact: Palma is the capital of Mallorca. Many people on the island speak Catalan as well as Spanish.

tasks.hint: Look at the word yo. It is happening now.
tasks.why: Happening now: estar + gerund. Estoy cocinando.

tasks.hint: Omar = él. It is happening now.
tasks.why: Estar with él: está hablando.

tasks.hint: Hablar is an -ar verb.
tasks.why: -ar verbs: -ando. Hablando.

tasks.hint: Comer is an -er verb.
tasks.why: -er and -ir verbs: -iendo. Comiendo.

tasks.hint: Ahora mismo means right now.
tasks.why: Right now: estar + gerund, never ser.

tasks.hint: Todos los días: is it happening now?
tasks.why: Every day: use the present, not the gerund.
Estar + gerund stay together: está esperando.

units.title: Say what you did today
claims: You say what you have done today.
You use ya and todavía no.

postcard.fact: The painter Pablo Picasso was born in Málaga in 1881.

tasks.hint: Look at the word yo.
tasks.why: Haber with yo: he. He ido.

tasks.hint: Ana is one person, not you.
tasks.why: Haber with él or ella: ha. Ha llegado.

tasks.hint: Hacer has an irregular participle.
tasks.why: Hacer → hecho. It does not follow -ido.

tasks.hint: Ver has an irregular participle.
tasks.why: Ver → visto.

tasks.hint: The person has paid. Is it done?
tasks.why: Already done: ya lo he pagado.

tasks.hint: The postman has not come. Maybe he comes later.
tasks.why: Not yet: todavía no.
Todavía no + he + participle.

units.title: Talk about last weekend
claims: You say what you did at the weekend.
You use ayer, anoche and the indefinido.

postcard.fact: Every August, people in Buñol throw tomatoes at each other. The festival is called La Tomatina.

tasks.hint: Ayer means yesterday. Look at the accents.
tasks.why: Ayer is the past: habló. Hablo means I speak.

tasks.hint: Todos los días, and the person is yo.
tasks.why: Every day, yo: trabajo. Trabajó is the past.

tasks.hint: Anoche means last night.
tasks.why: Anoche is the past, and él: llegó.

tasks.hint: Yesterday is finished.
tasks.why: Yesterday: indefinido. Ayer fui al banco.

tasks.hint: 2022 is a closed time.
tasks.why: A closed time: indefinido. En 2022 llegué.
Hacer is irregular: hiciste. ¿Qué hiciste?

units.title: Say how life was
claims: You say how life used to be.
You use antes: vivía, era, iba.

postcard.fact: Mérida has a Roman theatre about 2,000 years old. There are still plays here every summer.

tasks.hint: Antes: how things were, for a long time.
tasks.why: How things used to be: imperfecto. Antes vivía.

tasks.hint: What was she like, as a person?
tasks.why: What someone was like: ser. Mi abuela era simpática.

tasks.hint: Hay in the past has one form only.
tasks.why: Hay in the imperfecto is always había, even with tiendas.

tasks.hint: Antes … ahora: then and now.
tasks.why: Antes: trabajaba. Ahora: trabajo.

tasks.hint: Ayer, at nine o'clock: one finished event.
tasks.why: One finished event: indefinido. Ayer fui.
Antes usually goes first. Vivir with yo: vivía.
Hay in the past: había.

units.title: Don't repeat the word
claims: You replace a person or thing: lo veo.
You use me, lo, la, los, las.

postcard.fact: The great mosque of Córdoba has a cathedral inside it. People call the building the Mezquita.

tasks.hint: Tomás is one man.
Amina is one woman.
Mis padres: more than one person.
Ana is a person. Spanish adds a small word.
Llaves are things, not people. Do you need a?
Where does the pronoun go? Think: lo estoy…

units.title: Give things to people
claims: You say who gets something: le doy.
You use me, te, le, nos, les.

postcard.fact: The San Fermín festival in Pamplona starts on 6 July every year.

tasks.hint: Who gets the prescription? A mí.
tasks.why: A mí goes with me: me da una receta.

tasks.hint: Ana gets the email. One person.
tasks.why: The person who gets something: le, for a woman too.

tasks.hint: Your parents get the money. More than one.
tasks.why: More than one person who gets something: les.

tasks.hint: Is there a lo or a la after the gap?
tasks.why: No lo or la here, so: le doy las llaves.

tasks.hint: Look at the next word: la.
tasks.why: Le changes to se before lo, la, los, las: se la doy.

tasks.hint: Two pronouns. Can le stand before lo?
tasks.why: Le + lo is not possible. Le becomes se: se lo doy.
The pronoun goes before the verb: nos explican.

units.title: Say what you have to do
claims: You say tengo que, hay que and puedo.
You choose saber or poder.

postcard.fact: Logroño is the capital of La Rioja, a region famous for its wine.

tasks.hint: It is about me, this Saturday.
tasks.why: One person must: tener que. Tengo que trabajar.

tasks.hint: This is a rule for everyone.
tasks.why: Anyone must: hay que + infinitive.

tasks.hint: Mi marido y yo: two people you can name.
tasks.why: These two people must: tenemos que.

tasks.hint: Nunca he aprendido: never learned.
tasks.why: A skill you have learned: saber. No sé nadar.

tasks.hint: You can swim, but your arm hurts today.
tasks.why: Possible right now: poder. Hoy no puedo.
Hay que + infinitive: a rule for everyone.

units.title: Ask politely
claims: You ask politely: ¿Puede…? ¿Me pone…?
You say quería and me gustaría.

postcard.fact: The English word sherry comes from the name of this city, Jerez.

tasks.hint: You don't know the doctor well.
tasks.why: Someone you don't know well: usted. ¿Puede repetir?

tasks.hint: A polite way to say what you want.
tasks.why: In a bank or shop, quería is a polite “I'd like”.

tasks.hint: You would like to see the flat.
tasks.why: Me gustaría + infinitive = I would like to.

tasks.hint: You ask the waiter, using usted.
tasks.why: In Spain you order with ¿Me pone…? It is normal, not rude.

tasks.hint: ¿Te importa…? means “do you mind?”.
tasks.why: “Do you mind?” “No, I don't.” So you say no.
Quería + infinitive: a polite way to ask.

units.title: Say no
claims: You say: nada, nadie, nunca.
You use tampoco and ningún.

postcard.fact: The Spanish hero El Cid is buried in the cathedral of Burgos.

tasks.hint: It is about things in the fridge.
tasks.why: No things: nada.

tasks.hint: It is about people in the office.
tasks.why: No people: nadie.

tasks.hint: It is about how often you go.
tasks.why: No time: nunca.

tasks.hint: Before a masculine noun, this word gets shorter.
tasks.why: Before a masculine noun: ningún problema.

tasks.hint: Nadie comes before the verb.
tasks.why: Negative word before the verb: no second no.

tasks.hint: The first person says no. You agree.
tasks.why: After a negative sentence, agree with tampoco.
No + verb + a nadie. Use a before a person.

units.title: Say where things are
claims: You say where things are.
You use encima de, debajo de, al lado de.

postcard.fact: Many Western films were made in the Tabernas desert, near Almería.

tasks.hint: It is the opposite of “on top of”.
tasks.why: Under: debajo de. On top of: encima de.

tasks.hint: The word lado means side.
tasks.why: Next to: al lado de.

tasks.hint: We say el banco.
tasks.why: De + el = del.

tasks.hint: We say la cama.
tasks.why: De la does not join: debajo de la cama.

tasks.hint: One thing on each side. There is no de.
tasks.why: Between: entre, with no de. Entre el banco y el bar.
The thing, then están, then the place.

units.title: Tell a story
claims: You tell a story in the past.
You choose indefinido or imperfecto.

postcard.fact: Ronda stands on both sides of a deep gorge. A tall old bridge joins the two parts.

tasks.hint: A long time in your life, not one event.
tasks.why: Age and background: imperfecto. Cuando era pequeña.

tasks.hint: De repente: suddenly, one moment.
tasks.why: A sudden event: indefinido. Sonó.

tasks.hint: One action was in progress. Another one came.
tasks.why: In progress: cocinaba. The event that came: llamó.

tasks.hint: Moving to Spain happened once. It is finished.
tasks.why: One finished event in the past: me mudé.

tasks.hint: How did Ana feel at that moment?
tasks.why: A state, as background: estaba. Cansada goes with estar.

tasks.hint: Yo dormía is the scene. What happened then?
tasks.why: The scene: dormía. The event: sonó.
The imperfecto sets the scene. The indefinido brings the event.

units.title: Say what had happened
claims: You say what happened before something else.
You use había + participle: había salido.

postcard.fact: In 1812, a famous Spanish constitution was signed in Cádiz. People call it La Pepa.

tasks.hint: Look at the word ya. What came first?
tasks.why: It started before you arrived: había empezado.

tasks.hint: When did you leave the keys? Before or after?
tasks.why: First you left the keys, then you could not get in.

tasks.hint: First the exam, then the happy Omar.
tasks.why: The exam came first: había aprobado.

tasks.hint: Yo is the person. Does the participle change?
tasks.why: With haber, the participle always ends in -o: había estado.

tasks.hint: Escribir has an irregular participle.
tasks.why: Escribir → escrito: había escrito.
Había + participle stay together.

units.title: Talk about the future
claims: You say what will happen: lloverá, tendremos.
You make promises: te llamaré.

postcard.fact: The Tower of Hercules in A Coruña is a Roman lighthouse. It still works today.

tasks.hint: Mañana is tomorrow.
tasks.why: Tomorrow: futuro. Infinitive + -á: lloverá.

tasks.hint: A promise from yo, for tonight.
tasks.why: Yo in the futuro: -é after the infinitive. Llamaré.

tasks.hint: Venir has a short stem in the future.
tasks.why: Venir → vendr-: vendrá.

tasks.hint: Tener has a short stem in the future.
tasks.why: Tener → tendr-: tendremos.

tasks.hint: There will be a meeting. What is hay in the future?
tasks.why: Hay in the futuro: habrá.
Volveré dentro de una hora: dentro de = in, from now.

units.title: Sort out your flat
claims: You ask politely: me gustaría, ¿podría…?
You give advice: yo que tú, deberías.

postcard.fact: The Altamira Cave, near Santillana del Mar, has paintings more than 14,000 years old.

tasks.hint: It is a polite wish now, not the past.
tasks.why: A polite wish about now: me gustaría.

tasks.hint: What you would like is one action: visitar.
tasks.why: Before an infinitive, gustaría stays singular, even with nos.

tasks.hint: You speak politely to usted.
tasks.why: A polite request with usted: ¿podría…?

tasks.hint: Yo que tú: if I were you.
tasks.why: Yo que tú + conditional: le escribiría.

tasks.hint: Yo en tu lugar: advice for now.
tasks.why: Yo en tu lugar + conditional: no firmaría.
Me gustaría + infinitive: a polite wish.

units.title: Tell people what to do
claims: You tell someone what to do: firme aquí.
You tell people what not to do.

postcard.fact: Teruel is famous for its Mudéjar towers, built in a style with Islamic and Christian roots.

tasks.hint: You speak to your mother, using tú.
tasks.why: Tú, -ar verb: apaga.

tasks.hint: You speak to Señora, using usted.
tasks.why: Usted, -ar verb: the ending changes to -e. Firme.

tasks.hint: A formal message, using usted. Think of traigo.
tasks.why: From traigo, usted: traiga.

tasks.hint: A negative command with tú.
tasks.why: No + subjunctive: no llegues.

tasks.hint: A negative command with usted.
tasks.why: No + subjunctive, usted: no fume.

tasks.hint: A positive command with tú. Where does me go?
tasks.why: Positive command: the pronoun joins the end, with an accent.
Negative command: the pronouns go before the verb.

units.title: Talk about a problem
claims: You say what you want others to do.
You say how you feel: me molesta que.

postcard.fact: Tarragona has a Roman amphitheatre right beside the sea.

tasks.hint: After quiero que you need the subjunctive.
tasks.why: Quiero que + subjunctive: me ayudes.

tasks.hint: After necesito que you need the subjunctive.
tasks.why: Necesito que + subjunctive: -ar verbs change to -e. Firme.

tasks.hint: A feeling comes first: me molesta que.
tasks.why: After a feeling, use the subjunctive: ponga.

tasks.hint: A feeling comes first: siento que.
tasks.why: Siento que + subjunctive: no puedas.

tasks.hint: Creo que: you think it is true.
tasks.why: Creo que + indicative: está.

tasks.hint: Espero que: it is a hope, not a fact.
tasks.why: Espero que + subjunctive: esté.
Me molesta que + subjunctive: llegues.

units.title: Describe people and places
claims: You describe people and things more exactly.
You use que, donde and lo que.

postcard.fact: Ávila is still surrounded by its medieval walls. You can walk along part of them.

tasks.hint: It is about a person: la chica.
tasks.why: People and things: que.

tasks.hint: Something happened in this place.
tasks.why: Something happens in the place: donde.

tasks.hint: There is no noun before the gap.
tasks.why: No noun: lo que = what, the thing that.

tasks.hint: The office itself does the action: está, cierra.
tasks.why: The place is the subject: que.

options: El barrio donde vivo es tranquilo.
El barrio que vivo es tranquilo.
tasks.hint: You live in that place.
tasks.why: Something happens in the place: donde vivo.
No noun: lo que. Lo que necesito es…

units.title: Ask for information
claims: You ask: ¿Puede decirme…? ¿Sabes cuándo…?
You report what people say and ask.

postcard.fact: Miguel de Cervantes, who wrote Don Quixote, was born in Alcalá de Henares.

tasks.hint: The direct question is yes/no: ¿Tiene la tarjeta?
tasks.why: A yes/no question: si, with no accent.

tasks.hint: You mean: where? It is still a question word.
tasks.why: An indirect question keeps the accent: dónde.

tasks.hint: You mean: which documents?
tasks.why: A question word keeps the accent: qué documentos.

tasks.hint: The direct question is: ¿Necesito cita previa?
tasks.why: A yes/no question: si, with no accent.

options: Ana me pregunta si dónde trabajas.
tasks.hint: Ana asked you. So now the verb is about you.
tasks.why: Dónde keeps its accent. Trabajas becomes trabajo, because it is you.
¿Puede decirme…? + the question word + the verb.
